answer: An agent marketplace requires a locked bond for every identity allowed to accept work, whether the job is checking a lantern, appraising an opal, or tracking a pulse. Bonds stay locked through a dispute window and are slashed when signed results fail an agreed, verifiable check. Creating more names adds no free capacity: an attacker running a thousand active identities must fund a thousand bonds, tie up that capital, and risk losing it for provable fraud.
